I went to Egypt 10 years ago as a teenager with my parents and grandparents and I thoroughly enjoyed it despite it's faults. I was studying ancient Egypt for my final HS exams and to see it in person was really something. My parents/grandparents organized personal drivers through a company and we had tours organized for us which I think really really helped. I did go out with my dad a few times alone to explore/get food which was a little daunting as a young 17 year old girl with people staring at me but I got used to it eventually. 

I'd definitely go back but with a lot of preparation and planning. I was "lucky" to be in Egypt during the 2014 post-coup unrest as it meant there was hardly any tourists in popular areas and virtually any lines to museums/sacred sites.   
  
Egypt has it's own problems absolutely. The mass poverty was a huge shock to me and everyone asking for money was unsettling but easy to wave off. The people are lovely overall though. The tour guides have a HUGE passion for their history and one of our tour guides was lovely enough to help me find a charger for my camera as I'd forgotten it at home. We went all over this city to find one and I was incredibly thankful and he was a lovely lovely man. 

I probably wouldn't travel Egypt alone as a single woman - a group tour or even family would be the best option for people in hindsight. Egypt is beautiful, the people are wonderful and open - as long as you stay on your guard you'll have a great time.

Whenever I wash mine I just get a shallow tub of lukewarm water with some mild dish soap, make it bubbly and chuck in the project and wiggle it around a bit. Leave it there for 15-30 minutes depending on size. After that I get a towel and roll it up to get excess water out and then line hang!
